dedupe_keys.name: imf portwatch port and chokepoint activity data

description: PortWatch is a platform and open data set for monitoring and simulating maritime trade disruptions. Its data sets include daily port calls and estimated import and export volumes by ship category (container, dry bulk, general cargo, ro-ro, tanker) for 2,065 ports, daily transit calls and trade volumes through maritime chokepoints, a ports database classifying ports as globally, regionally or domestically systemic, disruption events from GDACS, and spillover-simulator and climate-scenario layers informed by modelled cyclone, flood and earthquake risk at about 1,400 ports. Estimates are derived from satellite AIS vessel positions following Arslanalp, Koepke and Verschuur (IMF Working Paper 2021/225). It is a collaboration between the IMF and the University of Oxford Environmental Change Institute, developed with Esri, the UN Global Platform, the World Bank and the WTO and launched in beta on 15 November 2023. The daily port series runs from 1 January 2019 to within about a week of the present, with a change log of methodology revisions. Data are free under IMF terms of use, downloadable as CSV or GeoJSON and queryable through ArcGIS feature-service APIs. Caveats: trade volumes are model estimates from AIS, revised when vessels, ports or boundaries are added. PortWatch serves supply-chain cascading failure, resilience, emergency response and climate adaptation studies of ports, alongside the World Port Index catalogued here.
